title: Snapshotlets — session bookmarks & micro-replay (scratch)
content:
Context / why I care:
- We keep losing useful multi-turn context when debugging user issues or trying to reproduce regressions.
- Long session captures are heavy and expensive (storage + retrieval). Engineers and support want pin-pointable ‘moments’ inside a session to share and replay quickly.
- Idea: tiny, first-class session bookmarks ('snapshotlets') that capture: prompt prefix, model inputs, short kv-cache pointers (or hashed tokens), UI state, and optional user notes. Lightweight, searchable, shareable.

Problem statement:
- Support/SEs need to show customers what happened in a conversation without shipping entire logs.
- Engineers need deterministic minimal repros for failures/regressions.
- PMs want ability to A/B exact micro-conversations as part of rollout QA.

Primary goals (MVP):
1) UX: quick bookmark action in console/session viewer (keyboard shortcut + button).
2) Data: store immutable snapshotlet record with stable id, timestamp, tags, short text summary (<= 512 tokens).
3) Replay: open snapshotlet to replay the short context into a dev sandbox (or into a read-only console).
4) Share: generate link with role-scoped access (view-only for external), integrates with audit logs.
5) Cost: store only metadata + minimal compressed context; default TTL 90 days with easy export-to-blob.

User personas / example jobs-to-be-done:
- Support Engineer: "I want to capture the exact exchange where the model hallucinated an address so I can send a compact repro to the model team."
- ML Engineer: "I want deterministic inputs to run a comparator eval across quantized vs full models."
- Product Manager: "I want to pin a few customer screenshots/conversations for post-mortem and for feature acceptance."

User stories (rough):
- As a support engineer, when viewing a user session, I can select 1–5 turns and create a snapshotlet with a short note and tags.
- As an ML engineer, I can load a snapshotlet into an integration test harness to run it against multiple model variants and record outputs.
- As a PM, I can create a collection of snapshotlets to attach to a rollout as acceptance tests.

Data model (sketch, keep simple):
- snapshotlet_id (uuid)
- created_by
- created_at
- session_id (optional)
- turn_range (start_turn, end_turn)
- prompt_text (string, trimmed to X tokens)
- input_meta (model_name, temperature, top_p, embeddings_enabled)
- kv_hash (short hex of saved KV state) OR pointer to prefix cache blob
- ui_state (selected user message, attachments refs)
- tags, note
- access_policy (public/team/internal)

Implementation notes / risks:
- Security: snapshotlets may contain PII. Default: redact PII heuristics + require SSA for external links.
- Size: we must avoid capturing full kv-cache by default. Option: store hash + on-demand request to pull expanded trace if user is privileged.
- Cost: TTL + tiered storage (hot 30d, cold 90–365d, export for long term).
- Privacy: link-sharing must adhere to customer private deployment settings (if private deployment, snapshotlets must be stored in customer-controlled S3 or not at all).

UX rough flow (console):
- In session viewer: select turns -> right-click -> "Create snapshotlet" -> modal (title, tags, note, retention dropdown).
- After create: toast -> snapshotlet appears in sidebar collection -> actions: share link, open in sandbox, export JSON, delete.
- Keyboard shortcut: Cmd+K to create quick snapshot from last N turns (configurable default N=6).

Developer-facing replay flow:
- Sandbox loader API: POST /sandbox/load-snapshotlet {snapshotlet_id, target_model, override_params} -> returns run_id + logs.
- Should support 'replay-only' (non-billing) mode for triage; or mark it as billable if it actually triggers model runs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create snapshotlet from session selection -> persisted record with id and metadata.
- Console shows snapshotlets listing for a session and global listing for user.
- Replay in sandbox replays chosen turns in same order and returns deterministic tokenized inputs (within model nondeterminism limits).
- Share link resolves to read-only console with audit entries.
- Default retention policy applied and snapshotlet deletion audited.

Metrics / success signals:
- Adoption: snapshotlets per active monthly user, per support rep. Target: 3 snapshotlets per rep/month in first 3 months.
- Time-to-resolution: average time to close support ticket where snapshotlet was used vs without. Target: 20% faster.
- Storage cost: average bytes per snapshotlet <= 3KB metadata + <= 4KB compressed context.
- Replay failures: percent of snapshotlets that fail to replay (target <2%).

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0: internal alpha (core SEs + ML infra) — manual API + dev sandbox.
- Phase 1: internal beta in Console for company support org.
- Phase 2: public beta (hosted API customers opt-in) with link sharing.
- Phase 3: GA with retention controls exposed in billing.

Experiment ideas / followups:
- Auto-suggestion of snapshotlets: system recommends potential snapshotlets when it detects anomalous outputs (low confidence, safety flags, hallucination heuristics).
- Compact diffs: store a diff between original chat and snapshotlet to save space.
- Snapshotlet bundles + annotations for postmortems (allow threaded comments).

Open questions / discussion items for sync with infra:
- How to represent kv-cache pointers in a vendor-agnostic way? (hash + version + optional blob).
- Should replay always run against pinned model version? (probably yes for determinism).
- SLA and retention defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Audit log surfaces: link-sharing events need to be in high-fidelity audit trail.

Next steps (for next two weeks):
- Talk to Marco + Diana to map required backend endpoints and auth surface (sync Wed).
- Quick spike: implement minimal snapshotlet proto in session-store (store metadata + trimmed text) and a console-side UI prototype (mock).
- Draft short internal one-pager for support org with examples (2–3 repros).

Notes to self / rough todos:
- Save example ticket: customer A chat where doc link got hallucinated -> use as sample snapshotlet.
- Check privacy policy for external link sharing in private deployments.
- Put PRD skeleton in Confluence: link above.

Random brain-dump bits (leave here so I don't forget):
- Allow tagging with structured labels: 'prod-regression', 'hallucination', 'cost-spike'.
- Consider command-line snapshotlet export for SREs (cli: redwood snapshotlet export <id> --target s3).
- Throttle snapshotlet creation per user (to avoid abuse) and put quota in console.
- Copy to Github issue template generator for ML reproducibility.

End of scratch — iterate after sync.
